about: The Cosmic Atlas: one record per stage of the journey. The page reads its text, labels, sources and camera framing from here. Ages are years after the Big Bang as [earliest, latest]; null means the stage is not tied to one epoch. 'transition' says how the journey leaves a stage: a morph, a zoom in or out by 'depth' e-folds of scale, or 'out-in' (pull back to the 'via' stage, then dive by 'depth2'). 'clock' is the journey's own clock at that stage, in years after the Big Bang (stages not tied to one epoch still get a place on it); 'tempo' is what the clock says while resting there.

events.title: The beginning
events.label: model
events.scale: everything we can see, packed together
events.note: Our whole observable universe, hot and dense beyond imagining. Not an explosion into empty space: there is no outside. Space itself begins to expand, everywhere at once.
events.sound: a deep, slow om: a low drone that opens into a vowel and closes to a hum

events.title: Primordial energy
events.label: model
events.note: Hot, dense and almost uniform. Space itself is expanding, and tiny fluctuations will seed everything that follows. At 380,000 years the universe turns transparent.
events.sound: sub-bass drone, a growling filtered saw, grainy noise and a rising wall of harmonics

events.title: Structure emerges
events.label: observed
events.era: hundreds of millions of years on
events.note: The first glow fades and gravity works in the dark, drawing matter into filaments and nodes where the first stars ignite. Surveys map this web; the shape drawn here is procedural.
events.sound: glassy open fifths that shimmer, with a breath of high air

events.title: A city of galaxies
events.label: observed
events.note: The bright knot resolves into dozens of young galaxies with empty space between them, pulled together by gravity. Webb sees clusters like this forming, such as the Spiderweb.
events.sound: a quiet open pad with scattered bell notes, one per galaxy

events.title: A young galaxy blazes
events.label: observed
events.era: about 10 billion years ago, when quasars peaked
events.scale: tens of thousands of light-years, jets far beyond
events.note: Inside the cluster, one smudge up close: a young galaxy with giant clumps of new stars, tidal tails, and a core outshining everything, firing twin jets.
events.sound: a bright chord pulsing hard, a deep throb and a jet-like hiss

events.title: A galaxy like ours
events.label: observed
events.era: over the next several billion years
events.note: Mergers calm and the gas settles into a barred spiral like the Milky Way: a dense bulge, trailing arms that thin towards the edge, dust lanes on their inner sides, pink star-forming regions.
events.sound: a warm, slowly breathing D minor 9 pad

events.title: The dark heart
events.label: observed
events.era: at the centre of nearly every large galaxy
events.scale: ours fits inside Mercury's orbit; the largest outsize the solar system
events.note: A supermassive black hole: a ring of light round its shadow, a disc of hot gas, and stars whipping round it. The side of the disc turning towards us shines brighter. This view is procedural.
events.sound: a slow heartbeat at the edge of hearing, deep rumble, one eerie high tone

events.title: Pillars of creation
events.label: observed
events.note: Back in a spiral arm: pillars of cold gas and dust, eroded by hot young stars above. Hydrogen glows red, oxygen green-teal. New stars form in the dense tips.
events.sound: breathy, vowel-like noise, as if the pillars were singing, over a soft pad

events.title: A cloud collapses
events.label: observed
events.era: 4.6 billion years ago, for our Sun
events.note: One knot falls in on itself. Spin steers the falling gas onto a disc, where it lands in a flash, while the newborn star fires jets from its poles into glowing shock fronts.
events.sound: a low saw straining against a closing filter, the hiss of infall

events.title: Fusion ignites
events.label: model
events.era: when the core nears 15 million degrees
events.scale: atomic nuclei, a million-billionth of a metre across
events.note: In the core, hydrogen nuclei repel each other until heat and pressure force some close enough to fuse, each fusion releasing energy. When the burn holds steady, a star is born.
events.tempo: slowed enormously: real nuclei meet in an instant
events.sound: a low hum under a quickening crackle of bright notes, one for each fusion

events.title: A new star shines
events.label: observed
events.note: The new star lights the disc of dust around it, which settles into rings and gaps like those ALMA imaged around the young star HL Tauri.
events.sound: the first major chord, bright and warm

events.title: A giant like Jupiter
events.label: model
events.era: while the young disc is still rich in gas
events.note: Beyond the frost line giants form while gas is plentiful. Jupiter's ten-hour spin pulls its clouds into belts and zones flowing opposite ways. Saturn is shown with today's rings, which may be young.
events.tempo: one ten-hour day every two minutes
events.sound: a deep organ-like fifth that beats slowly, with banded winds blowing across it

events.title: The Moon is born
events.label: model
events.era: about 4.5 billion years ago, as the Earth finished forming
events.scale: Earth, and an impactor the size of Mars
events.note: A Mars-sized world, Theia, strikes the young Earth a glancing blow. Molten debris circles the planet and gathers into the Moon: in hours or over centuries, models differ. Distances are compressed.
events.tempo: hours at first, then years, each second
events.sound: a slow tolling over a low rumble of molten rock

events.title: Worlds form
events.label: model
events.era: the next 100 million years or so
events.note: Dust drifts along each ring and gathers into clumps that grow into planets: small rocky ones close in, giants beyond the frost line. Sizes are exaggerated.
events.sound: a slow music-box arpeggio over a soft pad, like orbits ticking round

events.title: The star sheds its shell
events.label: model
events.era: about 5 billion years from now, for our Sun
events.note: Our Sun will swell into a red giant like pi1 Gruis, its surface a few enormous boiling cells. It will swallow Mercury and Venus, perhaps Earth, but not Mars.
events.sound: low, slow and swelling: a minor third that sighs

events.title: The universe looks back
events.label: observed
events.era: about 5 billion years from now; the Helix shows it today
events.note: The star sheds its outer layers in waves. Its bare core, a white dwarf, lights them from within. The Helix Nebula, 650 light-years away, is a real one; the eye is our reading.
events.sound: resolution: a still D major 9 with high shimmer
